summary: Defines an RTCP Source Description item and an RTCP Extended Report block that identify and describe a measurement period. Other XR blocks can refer to this period. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: RTCP reports carry quality numbers about a media stream, such as how many packets were lost. RFC 6776 adds a small block that names the time window those numbers cover, so many small metric blocks can share one identity instead of repeating it.

questions: how to identify measurement period in rtcp
what is rtcp measurement information block
what is the apsi sdes item
subtitle: Lets RTCP reports name the measurement period and stream they describe, so separate metric blocks can share one identity.

tldr.problem: RTCP Extended Report blocks report measurements such as packet loss, but a receiver cannot tell which time window or which part of a stream a number came from. Every metric block would otherwise have to repeat that information.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6776 adds an Application-Specific Identifier SDES item and a Measurement Information XR block. The block names the first and last packet of the measurement and gives its duration, so other metric blocks can point back to one shared identity.
tldr.outcome: The result is a single place in an RTCP packet that ties measurement results to a stream and a period. The RFC is a Proposed Standard from October 2012 and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 6776 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2012. It has not been obsoleted and nothing in the unit metadata updates it, so it remains the definition of the Measurement Identity SDES item and the Measurement Information XR block.

sections.title: Naming the Measurement Period
sections.content:
RTCP is the reporting side of RTP, the protocol that carries live media. Reports arrive as packets that describe how a stream is doing. RFC 6776 adds two new pieces to that reporting: a Source Description (SDES) item and an Extended Report (XR) block.

Neither new piece carries a measurement result. Instead they carry the information needed to interpret results found in other blocks, namely the sequence number of the first packet of the RTP session, the extended sequence numbers of the first packet of the current measurement interval and of the last packet included in the measurement, the duration of the most recent measurement interval, and the duration of the interval that applies to cumulative measurements. That last duration may be the length of the RTP session so far.

The reason for a shared identity is overhead. Commonly several small metric blocks report on the same stream and the same period. If each one carried its own copy of the identifying data, the reports would grow much larger than the results they hold.
sections.plainLanguage: Quality reports about a media stream need to say which stream and which stretch of time they cover. RFC 6776 puts that information in one shared place so many small reports can point to it instead of repeating it.

sections.title: How RTCP Reports Are Built
sections.content:
RTCP reporting is defined in RFC 3550. RFC 3611 defines the extensible structure used for reporting through an RTCP XR, and defines the XR blocks themselves. RFC 6776 adds one new XR block to that structure.

The SDES item provides a field for an application-specific auxiliary identifier. Such an identifier may be used to correlate data in XR blocks within an RTP session with data from a non-RTP session. An RTCP Measurement Identity SDES packet may be associated with a set of RTCP XR metric blocks that share the same application-specific measurement identifier.

A single RTCP packet may hold several such sets, each with its own shared information. A packet may also hold XR blocks that are not associated with any Measurement Information block, for example blocks that were defined before this mechanism existed. The XR block carrying the measurement information does not have to appear in the same RTCP packet as the SDES item carrying the measurement identity.
sections.plainLanguage: Reports are built from small blocks. This RFC adds one block that holds the shared identity, and one source-description item that holds an identifier for the application. Other blocks may sit in the same packet without being tied to that identity.

sections.title: The Application-Specific Identifier Item
sections.content:
The SDES item is carried in the RTCP SDES packet, whose format is defined in Section 6.5 of RFC 3550. Each SDES packet has a header with fixed-length fields for version, source count, packet type (PT) and length, followed by zero or more SDES items. In the SDES packet the PT field is set to SDES (202).

The new item is called APSI, the Application-Specific Identifier. Its header is one octet for the item type, whose value is 10, and one octet for the length of the identifier that follows. The identifier itself is variable length, and the value of the length field does not include the two-octet SDES item header.

The identifier is an extra label that is useful in the context of a specific application, for example an MPEG-2 transport identifier. Applications that are not configured to make use of the item MUST ignore it.
sections.plainLanguage: The new source-description item carries a short label that only the application understands. It starts with a type number of 10 and a length byte. Programs that do not use it are told to skip it.

sections.title: The Measurement Information Block
sections.content:
The new XR block is identified by the constant 14 in its Block Type (BT) field. It carries a one-octet reserved field that senders MUST set to zero and receivers ignore, a two-octet block length, the SSRC (synchronization source) of the stream source, another reserved field of 16 bits, the first sequence number, the extended first and last sequence numbers of the interval, and two duration fields.

The block length is the length of the report block in 32-bit words minus one. For the Measurement Information Block the block length is equal to 7.

The block is a container only. It holds no packet counts, no loss figures and no delay values. Its job is to make the results in other blocks interpretable.
sections.plainLanguage: The new report block has type number 14 and a fixed length of 7. It holds no results of its own. It holds the names and the times that make other blocks' results meaningful.

sections.title: What Each Field Measures
sections.content:
The first sequence number is the RTP sequence number of the first received RTP packet of the session. It is used to work out how many packets contributed to the cumulative measurements.

The extended first sequence number of interval and the extended last sequence number are the extended RTP sequence numbers of the first received packet of the current measurement interval and of the last packet that contributed to the measurement. An extended sequence number is expressed as the low 16-bit value containing the sequence number received in an RTP data packet plus the most significant 16-bit value containing the corresponding count of sequence number cycles. The calculation method is provided in RFC 3550.

The Measurement Duration (Interval) field is 32 bits and gives the duration of the reporting interval that applies to interval reports using this block, in units of 1/65536 seconds. The Measurement Duration (Cumulative) field is 64 bits and gives the duration of the reporting interval that applies to cumulative reports. It uses a 64-bit NTP-format timestamp as defined in RFC 5905: an unsigned fixed-point number with the integer part in the first 32 bits and the fractional part in the last 32 bits. A receiver of the media stream can compute either duration from the packets it receives, or by using the RTCP method described in RFC 3550.
sections.plainLanguage: The block names the first and last packet of the measured stretch, using sequence numbers that keep counting past the 16-bit rollover. Two counters give the length of that stretch: one in units of 1/65536 of a second, and one as a 64-bit NTP-style timestamp.

sections.title: Registered Values
sections.content:
A new SDES item type for RTCP SDES and a new XR block type for RTCP XR have been registered with IANA. For general guidelines on IANA considerations the RFC points to RFC 3550 for RTCP SDES and RFC 3611 for RTCP XR.

The Measurement Identity SDES item is added to the IANA "RTP SDES item types" registry with the abbreviation APSI, the name Application-Specific Identifier and the value 10. The block type value 14 in the IANA "RTCP XR Block Type Registry" is assigned to the Measurement Information Block.
sections.plainLanguage: Two numbers were reserved for this: item type 10 in the SDES registry and block type 14 in the XR block registry. Those are the values a sender puts on the wire.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RTCP reports can contain sensitive information, including information about the nature and duration of a session established between two or more endpoints. Because of that, the security mechanisms that apply to RTP, as documented in Section 9 of RFC 3550, also apply here.
sections.plainLanguage: These reports can reveal what kind of session took place and how long it lasted. The RFC therefore points at the RTP security rules instead of inventing new ones.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the variable-length identifier that follows, not counting this two-octet header.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: MUST be set to zero by senders and ignored by receivers.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: The synchronization source of the stream source.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: MUST be set to zero by senders and ignored by receivers.

fields.name: First Sequence Number
fields.desc: RTP sequence number of the first received RTP packet of the session.

fields.name: Extended First Sequence Number of Interval
fields.desc: Extended sequence number of the first packet of the current measurement interval.

fields.name: Extended Last Sequence Number
fields.desc: Extended sequence number of the last packet included in the measurement.

fields.name: Measurement Duration (Interval)
fields.desc: Reporting interval for interval reports, in units of 1/65536 seconds.

fields.name: Measurement Duration (Cumulative)
fields.desc: Reporting interval for cumulative reports, as a 64-bit NTP-format timestamp.
